Read a downloaded official Bank of Japan bulk ZIP or CSV

Source: R/bulk.R
read_boj_bulk.Rd

Parses a local bulk response or a boj_file from download_boj_bulk(). Headerless four-column Flow-of-Funds/Tankan long files and named wide CSV matrices are accepted. ZIP traversal, entry count, uncompressed size, individual member size, and CSV row count are bounded before the result is retained in memory.

Usage

read_boj_bulk(
  path,
  encoding = "UTF-8",
  max_entries = 1000L,
  max_uncompressed_bytes = 1024^3,
  max_member_bytes = 512 * 1024^2,
  max_rows = 2000000L
)

Arguments

path

A local regular ZIP/CSV path, or the length-one boj_file returned by download_boj_bulk(). The file is read as bytes to detect a ZIP signature; its filename extension is not trusted.

encoding

Character encoding passed to readr::read_csv() for CSV text, such as "UTF-8" or "CP932". It must name an encoding supported by the local R installation.

max_entries

Positive integer maximum number of ZIP members. The default is 1000L.

max_uncompressed_bytes

Positive maximum total uncompressed ZIP member bytes. The default is 1024^3 (1 GiB).

max_member_bytes

Positive maximum uncompressed bytes for one ZIP member. The default is 512 * 1024^2 (512 MiB).

max_rows

Positive integer maximum rows retained from each CSV. The default is 2000000L; one extra row is read to detect an over-limit file.

Value

For a CSV, a base data.frame whose columns are the parsed CSV columns and whose values are read as character. A headerless four-column file is named series_code, frequency, period, and value, then gets value_numeric (numeric conversion, with non-numeric values as NA) and value_status (the original "", "NA", or "ND" marker, otherwise "observed"). For a ZIP containing one CSV, the same data frame is returned with a source_file column. For a ZIP containing multiple CSVs, a named list of those data frames is returned with classes c("boj_bulk", "list"); names are the archive member paths and each table has its source_file. Every result has a readboj_provenance() attribute with the source hash/bytes, parser name and schema, encoding, and, for ZIPs, selected member names and total uncompressed bytes.

Details

This is an offline local parser: it makes no network request and does not update the readboj cache. ZIP members must be regular safe paths; absolute paths, drive-letter paths, and .. traversal are rejected. Only .csv members are extracted, into a temporary directory removed on exit; non-CSV ZIP members are ignored. The parser preserves text identifiers, labels, units, and suppression markers rather than guessing numeric types.

Missing or non-regular paths, unsupported parameters, unsafe archive paths, absent CSV members, and configured size/row bounds are checked by the package and produce typed readboj errors where applicable. Low-level malformed ZIP/CSV input or unsupported encoding may instead retain a base-R or dependency error or warning. A ZIP with no CSV members is rejected. This function does not infer a common schema across files or reconcile publication revisions.

See also

download_boj_bulk(), read_boj_workbook(), boj_provenance()

Examples

local({
  csv <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  on.exit(unlink(csv), add = TRUE)
  writeLines(c(
    "series_code,frequency,period,value",
    "SYNTHM01,MONTHLY,202601,101.5",
    "SYNTHM01,MONTHLY,202602,NA"
  ), csv)
  parsed <- read_boj_bulk(csv, max_rows = 10L)
  parsed[c("series_code", "period", "value_numeric", "value_status")]
})
#>   series_code period value_numeric value_status
#> 1    SYNTHM01 202601         101.5     observed
#> 2    SYNTHM01 202602            NA           NA
